title: rush-2002-world
label: Brock Newbludd

won.source: The fed's own title log (its written summary: 'Brock Newbludd defeats Chris Matthews on 8/29/2002 at Adrenaline 14.'), the match it was won in, and the ring announcer's own introduction in that match's text

lost.source: The fed's own title log's vacancy entry, which names the show (Adrenaline 21), the match ("Title declared vacant") and the day (18 October 2002); the same fact is on the fed's own site page: "Title declared vacant on 10/18/02 by Sylkk at Adrenaline 21"

note: Two defences are on record that the fed's own title log does not carry. First, the card of Adrenaline 16 (12 Sep 2002): he beat Tyler Valentine by pinfall in a match Sheila Tyrone introduces as "for the RUSH WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT TITLE", and the next show's recap segment names it too. Second, on a show with no card on file: the fed's own news post of 13 Oct 2002 says "Brock Newbludd defended his World Title against Tyler Valentine and Chris Matthews" at Rising From the Ashes. The fed's own news post of 21 Oct calls Newbludd "the 3rd ex-RUSH champ", which is what this chain makes him. The fed's own title log ends with the vacancy: the fed's own news post of 20 Oct has a World Title tournament "underway this week on Adrenaline 22" with its final booked for RUSH's December pay-per-view, and the fed's own title list names no later World champion. The card of Decimation 2002 (22 Dec 2002), the December pay-per-view PCW and RUSH staged together, has the match for the vacant title, and Tyler Valentine won it; the title log and the card disagree, and both are recorded (#sources-disagree).

title: rush-2002-syndicate
label: Statuz Quo

won.source: The fed's own title log (its written summary: 'Statuz Quo defeats Brock Newbludd in a Ladder Match on 5/23/2002 at Adrenaline 4.'), the match it was won in, and the ring announcer's own introduction in that match's text

lost.source: the next reign on the same page (Syndicate No. 2, El Spiffy!, 8/18/2002 at Crossroads) begins here; the fed's own title log is the match it changed hands in

note: The champion renamed the belt, in character, for the length of his reign. On the card of Adrenaline 5 (30 May 2002) he announces it himself: "I deserve not da 'Syndicate title' but my own! Datz why I'm officially renamin' da title to da \"Quo title\" fo' as long as my reign as champion!!", with a custom platinum belt unveiled on camera and a champion-declared stipulation, "from now on, diz title will only be defended in no disqualification matches". He repeats it on Adrenaline 10: "I am the QUO CHAMPION!!". This is not a second belt and not a rename by the federation: the announce team calls it degrading the Syndicate title, the fed's own title list keeps the name Syndicate Championship, the page heads its list "Syndicate Championship", and the next champion's own words are "how long it took for El Spiffy! to get the Quo-stink off of the belt". Three defences are on held cards, none in the fed's own title log: Ignition 2002 (16 Jun 2002, beat Christopher Shackelton in a match announced "for one fall with no disqualifications and is for the Syndicate title", his own declared stipulation honoured), Adrenaline 8 (27 Jun 2002; he lost the match by disqualification and kept the belt, the card's words being "Winner by DQ: Steve Brent. Statuz Quo retains his Syndicate Title") and Adrenaline 11 (25 Jul 2002, beat Caleb McGlocklan by pinfall). A fourth match is explicitly not a title match: on Adrenaline 10 Sheila Tyrone introduces "a non-title match", which Statuz Quo lost to William 'Biohazard' Perry. The page's "Longest Title Holder: Statuz Quo-87 days" agrees exactly with 23 May to 18 August.

title: rush-2002-syndicate
label: El Spiffy!

won.source: The fed's own title log (its written summary: 'El Spiffy! defeats Statuz Quo with Caleb McGlocklan as special referee on 8/18/2002 at Crossroads.'), the match it was won in, and the ring announcer's own introduction in that match's text

note: Five defences are on held cards, none in the fed's own title log, each announced as a Syndicate title match: Adrenaline 14 (29 Aug 2002; he lost the match and kept the belt, the ring announcer's words being "Your winner, due to interference, Scott Cage! But still the Syndicate Champion, El Spiffy!"), Adrenaline 15 (5 Sep 2002, beat Wes Outlett), Adrenaline 16 (12 Sep 2002, beat Chris Matthews), Adrenaline 17 (19 Sep 2002, a four-way over Chris Matthews, The Masked Mullet and Caleb McGlocklan) and Adrenaline 19 (4 Oct 2002, retained when Stimpo was disqualified). The belt itself was stolen twice and the championship never moved: Stimpo impersonated him to hand himself the belt on Adrenaline 18, the CEO Rush Mason took it back and voided it on screen ("it's a good thing you were just joking about that whole 'giving the belt away' thing... So why don't you just keep this belt for now"), the real El Spiffy! was found tied up backstage, and Stimpo laid him out and took the belt again on Adrenaline 19. A sixth defence is the WCW Hardcore match at Rising From the Ashes (13 Oct 2002), booked on the card of Adrenaline 19 (he challenges Stimpo "to a match at the Pay-Per-View! For HIS Spiffy-cate title"); the fed's own pay-per-view script, served as a document, has Sheila Tyrone announce "here is your winner, and STILL RUSH Wrestling Syndicate Champion, EL SPIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIFFYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYY" and James Williams say he returned "JUST A DAY AFTER BEING HOSPITALIZED FOR A BACK INJURY" to defend it. The reign ended after the fed's own record, which carries no later Syndicate change and whose title list (about October 2002) still names him champion: the PCW card of Turmoil 102 (3 Dec 2002) has Stimpo "winning his first title, the Syndicate Title on Sunday Adrenaline defeating both Ebola III and Spiffy! in their triple threat match" (the Adrenaline of Sunday 1 Dec 2002, on no capture), and Decimation 2002's commentary says "Even when he lost his belt, Stimpo pinned Ebola in the triple threat to end it!" and that he held "the belt for 107 days"; 18 Aug to 1 Dec 2002 is 105 days; the commentary's count and the calendar differ, and no length is claimed.

lost.source: The PCW card of Turmoil 102 (3 Dec 2002): Stimpo's first title, "the Syndicate Title on Sunday Adrenaline defeating both Ebola III and Spiffy! in their triple threat match"; the Sunday before that card is 1 Dec 2002 and its Adrenaline card is on no capture.

note: SOURCES DISAGREE. The fed's own written summary of the change and its Title History page both date it "on 9/5/2002 at Adrenaline 16", and the fed's own booking record puts Adrenaline 16 on 12 Sep 2002 (5 Sep 2002 is Adrenaline 15). Both readings stand. The change is dated 12 Sep 2002, because the title match is on the card of Adrenaline 16 (Livewire, Tyronne Sharper and G.O.D. in a triple threat, won by Livewire) and the page's line names the right show and the wrong day, or the right day and the wrong show, and cannot be both. No length is given for this reign or for the next, because of the disagreement. One defence is on a held card, not in the fed's own title log: Adrenaline 14 (29 Aug 2002), announced "for the RUSH Network Championship"; he beat Livewire by pinfall, the man who would take the belt from him a fortnight later.

note: SOURCES DISAGREE. The fed's own written summary of the change and its Title History page both date it "on 9/5/2002 at Adrenaline 16", and the fed's own booking record puts Adrenaline 16 on 12 Sep 2002 (5 Sep 2002 is Adrenaline 15). Both readings stand. The change is dated 12 Sep 2002, because the title match is on the card of Adrenaline 16 and the page's line names the right show and the wrong day, or the right day and the wrong show, and cannot be both. No length is given for the previous reign or this one's start, because of the disagreement. Two defences are on record, neither in the fed's own title log. First, Adrenaline 18 (27 Sep 2002), announced "for the RUSH NETWORK TITLE": the billed challenger Stimpo never appeared and Joe Bananas attacked the champion instead; the card gives no result and none is claimed, and the belt did not change hands. Second, Rising From the Ashes (13 Oct 2002; the fed's own pay-per-view script, served as a document): Sheila Tyrone announces "the RUSH Network Title", Livewire beats Joe Bananas with the Electricity ("Winner: Livewire", "LIVEWIRE KEEPS THE NETWORK TITLE!"), and the fed's own newsdesk has it in Bananas's own words, "Ah lost ta Livewire at Rising From the Ashes". The reign ended after the fed's own record: the fed's own title log carries no later Network change and its own title list (about October 2002) still names him champion, but the PCW card of Fusion 101 (20 Dec 2002) has Matt Hunt walk out with "his newly acquired Network Title", saying he won it "last week on Turmoil", and the commentary calls Livewire "past his prime" (reign r005); how Livewire lost it is on no served card.

lost.source: Matt Hunt's own account on the PCW card of Fusion 101 (20 Dec 2002), "my wunderbar title win last week on Turmoil" (Turmoil 103, 10 Dec 2002, whose served card shows no title match); see the next reign.

title: rush-2002-world
label: Tyler Valentine

won.source: The served Decimation 2002 card (promotions/pcw/archive/pcw-decimation-2002-2002-12-22.html): the ring announcer introduces the match as "…AND IS FOR THE VACANT RUSH WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP!" and closes it "YOUR WINNER, AND NEW RUSH WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION… TYLER VALENTINEEEEEE!"

note: The fed's own title log and the cards disagree, and both are recorded (#sources-disagree). The fed's own title log stops at the vacancy of 18 October 2002 and its own title list names no World champion after Brock Newbludd. The pay-per-view card of Decimation 2002, staged by PCW and RUSH together, has the match for the vacant title: the announcer's introduction above, the commentary "Two and a half months without a champion and we're finally going to have our rightful leader!", Tyler Valentine beating McGlocklan, and the announcer's closing call. The cards that follow bill him champion. Fusion 103 (3 Jan 2003) stages "Tyler Valentine's RUSH World Championship coronation" and introduces him as "the RUSH World Champion"; Turmoil 107 (7 Jan 2003) introduces him as "the RUSH World Heavyweight Champion"; Shanghaied III (26 Jan 2003) bills "Tyler Valentine (c) vs Marvin Harris" for the RUSH World title, the announcer introduces him as "the RUSH World Heavyweight Champion", and the match ends with the announcer's "YOUR WINNER, AND STILL RUSH WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAM—" cut off by Valentine, who finishes the call himself. No card on file shows the belt leaving him: none of the PCW cards on file dated after Shanghaied III (the Turmoil and Fusion cards of 28 Jan 2003 onward, March Madness, Spring Fling and Supremacy 2003, Shanghaied IV and the Turmoil cards to 17 Apr 2004) names him or the RUSH World title, so the reign carries no end date and none is claimed.

title: rush-2002-network
label: Matt Hunt

won.source: His own account on the PCW card of Fusion 101 (/promotions/pcw/archive/pcw-fusion-101-2002-12-20.html, 20 Dec 2002): he walks out with "his newly acquired Network Title" and says "I want to be the first one to congratulate myself on my wunderbar title win last week on Turmoil"; the Turmoil of the week before is Turmoil 103 (10 Dec 2002), whose served card shows no title match, so the date is that Turmoil's and the match itself is on no served card. Turmoil 104 (17 Dec 2002) introduces him as "the RUSH Network Champion", and on Fusion 101 he calls that match his "first…and may I add successful…title defense".

note: The fed's own title log, whose page dates from about October 2002, ends with Livewire's reign, before this one; this reign is on PCW's cards of December 2002 and January 2003. Four defences are on served cards: Turmoil 104 (17 Dec 2002, Matt Hunt (c) against Ariz Ona, Gideon Poe special referee, announced as "for the RUSH Network Championship"; Poe stops it when Hunt uses a foreign object, "This match is a no contest. DDT hangs on to his title."), Decimation 2002 (22 Dec 2002, a German rules Christmas ladder match against Gideon Poe, "THE WINNER AND STILL RUSH NETWORK CHAMPION…MATT HUNT!!!"), Turmoil 107 (7 Jan 2003, against Stimpo, a count-out win for Stimpo: "STILL NETWORK CHAMPION, MATT HUNT!") and Shanghaied III (26 Jan 2003, against Stimpo, "YOUR WINNER AND STILLLLL RUSH NETWORK CHAMPION.... MATTHIAS KUNTZ-HUNT!"). On Turmoil 108 (14 Jan 2003) he is introduced as "the RUSH Network Champion" against Ebola III, the Syndicate champion, in a match billed for neither belt. The card of Sunday Adrenaline, 19 Jan 2003, announces that Stimpo has "a big Network Title Match one week from tonight". No PCW card dated after Shanghaied III (26 Jan 2003), from the Turmoil of 28 Jan 2003 to the cards of April 2004, bills a RUSH Network or Syndicate title or names its champion. The reign therefore carries no end date and none is claimed.
